props.note: the catalyst of the earlier kinetic work (refs. 1-4); its results are cited, not reported here

props.name: rate of the entering gas depends little on CO between 8 and 12%; higher CO lowers the rate; 12% CO chosen
props.statement: The reaction rate of entering gases containing 8 to 12% CO depends little on their composition; for higher CO content the rate decreases. 12% CO, 80% H2, 8% inert was chosen, corresponding to industrial practice.

props.name: at most 25-30% of the entering CO reacts per pass; at 300 atm hardly more than 25%
props.statement: At most only 25-30% of the CO entering the reactor reacts per pass; operating at 300 atm this percentage hardly exceeds 25%.

props.name: pore diffusion lowers effectiveness of the ZnO-Cr2O3 catalyst to about 0.5-0.7 at industrial conditions, in agreement with experiment
props.statement: Concentration gradients in the pores of the catalyst granules lower the effectiveness of the ZnO-Cr2O3 catalyst in industrial methanol reactors; for industrial operating conditions the effectiveness is calculated to be about 0.5-0.7, in agreement with experimental data.

props.name: effectiveness increases markedly with decreasing temperature, less with increasing conversion, and tends to one near equilibrium
props.statement: The effectiveness markedly increases with decreasing temperature and, to a lesser extent, with increasing conversion; approaching equilibrium (reaction rates tending to zero) it tends to one independently of temperature.

props.name: the highest rate is obtained at H2/CO above the stoichiometric 2
props.statement: The highest reaction rate is not obtained at the stoichiometric H2 to CO ratio of 2 but at a higher ratio, so the CO content of the feed gases is rather low.

props.name: interface heat and mass transfer effects are of opposite sign and tend to compensate
props.statement: The two mechanisms of heat and mass transfer in the interface area give effects which tend to compensate each other, because they are of opposite sign.

props.name: Hulbert's boundary condition y(0)=1 is inconsistent; its criterion overestimates
props.statement: The limiting condition used by Hulbert, y(z=0) = 1, is not consistent with the problem because it neglects the back-diffusion exerted by the reaction on molecules in the entry region; the criterion obtained by Hulbert therefore yields values that are too high.

props.name: laboratory kinetics (granules 0.6-0.9 mm, effectiveness 1) apply directly to industrial reactors
props.note: the kinetic results are cited from refs. 1-4 (Natta, Pino, Mazzanti, Pasquon)
props.statement: The laboratory kinetic data, obtained with 0.6-0.9 mm granules practically free of heat- and mass-transfer effects (effectiveness factor 1), can be directly applied to calculating industrial reactors.

props.name: unlike ammonia synthesis, methanol reactor design must account for secondary reactions
props.statement: Methanol and ammonia synthesis show remarkable physico-chemical analogies, but the absence of secondary reactions in ammonia synthesis allows its reactors to be calculated mainly from kinetic parameters, which is not so for methanol.

props.name: optimum: approximately isothermal 390-400 °C below 20% CO conversion, then decreasing to 390-395 °C; close to Italian reactors
props.statement: For a reactor at about 300 atm, taking kinetics and secondary reactions into account, the optimum is approximately isothermal (about 395 °C) over most of the bed: for conversions below 20% of the entering CO an isothermal curve between 390 and 400 °C, and only above about 20% a progressive decrease to 390-395 °C; some Italian industrial reactors operate under very similar conditions.

props.name: Knudsen and Poiseuille diffusion excluded at 300 atm with excess H2; ordinary diffusion occurs
props.statement: In the pores, Knudsen diffusion is excluded because the high pressure (300 atm) lowers the mean free path, Poiseuille diffusion is excluded by the high excess of hydrogen, and ordinary diffusion is the mechanism that occurs.

props.name: among the physical phenomena, pore diffusion most influences the reaction rate; other heat and mass transfer can be neglected
props.statement: Among all the physical phenomena, diffusion of the reactants in the pores of the catalyst granules most influences the reaction rate and decreases the effectiveness; the other mass- and heat-transfer phenomena in the bed can be neglected.

props.name: rate equation (1) of the earlier integral-reactor study on ZnO-Cr2O3 and ZnO-CuO-Cr2O3 catalysts (cited)
props.note: cited from refs. 1-4; equation read from the rendered page; A, B, C, D and K are given in the earlier papers
props.statement: The methanol synthesis rate from CO and H2 can be expressed by r = (f_CO p_CO f_H2^2 p_H2^2 - f_CH3OH p_CH3OH / K) / (A + B f_CO p_CO + C f_H2 p_H2 + D f_CH3OH p_CH3OH)^3, deduced from earlier studies in a practically isothermal integral reactor with catalysts based on ZnO-Cr2O3 and ZnO-CuO-Cr2O3.

props.name: reaction temperature kept below 410-420 °C: methanol purity decreases, and above 390-400 °C methane formation rises rapidly; catalyst aging also limits temperature
props.statement: The reaction temperature is kept below 410-420 °C because at the highest temperatures the purity of the methanol decreases, and temperatures above 390-400 °C cause a rapid increase of methane production from CO and H2, a reaction thermodynamically more favoured than methanol formation and highly exothermic, which can cause undesired temperature rises and methane excess in the recycle gas; lessening catalyst aging is another reason.

props.statement: The highest rate at H2/CO above 2 can be attributed to carbon monoxide being more adsorbable than hydrogen, so that gases rich in hydrogen are needed to obtain the maximum rate on the catalyst surface.

props.statement: For the effectiveness calculation the effective diffusivity in the pores is taken as Deff = θ D_m √2 (θ = 0.68), catalyst particles are isothermal with the same porous structure at all sizes and constant diffusivity, and the rate is linearized in CO because hydrogen is in large excess and the diffusion constants of CO and CH3OH are almost equal.
